description: What is a DJ, and what do DJs actually do? Learn how DJs select music, build sets, mix tracks, use equipment and develop their skills.
Explore the history of DJing, from radio disc jockeys and disco to hip-hop turntablism, house, techno, CDJs and modern digital DJ culture.
Explore the different types of DJs, from club and open-format DJs to wedding, radio, festival and turntablist performers. Compare their skills and roles.
Learn how DJ controllers, decks, mixers, cue headphones, audio interfaces and speakers work together, from source to master output.
Learn essential DJ terminology, from BPM, beatmatching and cue points to EQ, crossfaders, stems and DJ sets, with clear definitions and real examples.
Learn what BPM means in DJing, how tempo differs from rhythm and pulse, how to find a song's BPM, and why tempo matters when mixing tracks.
Learn to count beats and bars in 4/4 music, understand time signatures, accents and subdivisions, and apply counting to DJ mixing.
Learn song structure for DJing: identify intros, verses, choruses, pre-choruses, bridges, breakdowns, builds, drops and outros, then map tracks for better mixing.
Learn how to identify downbeats, strong and weak beats, backbeats, syncopation and audio transients by ear—and why these matter for beatgrids and DJ mixing.
Learn musical keys and scales for DJing: notes, semitones, intervals, major and minor scales, chords, relative keys and how DJs identify a track's key.
Learn how the Camelot Wheel works, what 8A and 8B mean, all 24 musical keys, compatible-key moves, DJ mixing examples and when not to follow the wheel.
Learn how DJs judge musical energy, loudness, intensity, dynamics and tension; map tracks, plan energy curves and build transitions that feel right.
Learn what groove and swing mean in music, how straight and swung beats differ, and how shuffle, syncopation and microtiming affect DJ mixing.
